comment: Scenes scripts/bench.mjs walks. Each becomes one page load per render
mode — DOM and canvas — because requestAnimationFrame has a single
cadence per document and two panes animating together would report the
page's fps rather than either mode's (bench/bench.ts explains it in full).
Every scene is a rigc gallery build under public/rigs/ (built by
and `many` walk-packed; a query's `rig` and `anim` name another build and
Counts are stepped because a single rig says nothing on a fast desktop
GPU: it pegs both modes at the display's refresh rate. The page caps
count at 64 (8 columns of 8, about 80 CSS px per cell at a 1280-wide
window); a denser grid would be measuring thumbnails. A rig's stage scale
is the scene's one-per-pane scale divided by the column count, so a step
raises the number of rigs rather than the amount of each one that is
`--corpus <dir>` points the script at a directory holding a file of this
shape plus the rigc builds it names (each query a `model` URL), for
real-world rigs that never enter this repository.

scenes.name: 1 meshed rig animating
scenes.why: the deform tier working every frame against the canvas mode's one-pass draw

scenes.name: 16 meshed rigs animating
scenes.why: an all-mesh grid — the canvas mode's home ground

scenes.name: 36 meshed rigs animating
scenes.why: between 16 and 64, so a crossover has somewhere to be seen rather than jumped over

scenes.name: 64 meshed rigs animating
scenes.why: the page's cap: the heaviest deform load either mode is asked for here

scenes.name: 1 meshed rig animating (canvas2d)
scenes.why: the DOM tier's default mesh backend, and the one real Safari struggles with

scenes.name: 16 meshed rigs animating (canvas2d)
scenes.why: the default backend under a grid — the per-triangle path's own scaling

scenes.name: 1 held pose
scenes.why: dirty-skip home ground: unchanged meshes reuse their raster, an unchanged frame is reused

scenes.name: 1 rigid rig animating
scenes.why: region attachments only — pure and one CSS matrix per slot on the DOM side

scenes.name: 16 rigid rigs animating
scenes.why: a grid of rigid rigs: element count and compositing against one canvas per rig

scenes.name: 64 rigid rigs animating
scenes.why: the cap, where the DOM side holds one element per drawn slot of 64 rigs (walk declares 15 slots)

scenes.name: 8 small players
scenes.why: independent players, each clipped to its own cell

scenes.name: 20 small players
scenes.why: past the browser's ~16-context cap: both modes share the package's one context
